blocks.title: Why start from EBIT and not net income?
blocks.teaser: UFCF is the cash available to all investors, before any payments to lenders.
blocks.body:
UFCF is the cash available to *all* investors, before any payments to lenders. Net income is already after interest, so it belongs only to equity.

**Interview answer:** "Unlevered cash flow is before debt payments, so we exclude interest by starting from EBIT."

blocks.title: Why tax EBIT rather than use actual taxes?
blocks.teaser: Actual taxes are reduced by the interest tax shield.
blocks.body: Actual taxes are reduced by the interest tax shield. In an unlevered DCF, the tax shield is captured in WACC (the after-tax cost of debt). Using actual taxes would count it twice.

blocks.prompt: In UFCF, why apply the tax rate to EBIT instead of using the company's actual taxes?

options.text: Actual taxes are hard to find
Actual taxes include the interest tax shield, which WACC already captures
EBIT is always higher than pre-tax income

blocks.explanation: Using actual taxes would count the interest tax shield twice — once in the cash flows and once in the after-tax cost of debt in WACC.

blocks.title: Unlevered vs. levered FCF?
blocks.teaser: Unlevered: before interest and debt repayments, available to all investors, discounted at WACC → EV.
blocks.body: Unlevered: before interest and debt repayments, available to all investors, discounted at WACC → EV. Levered: after interest and mandatory debt repayments, available to shareholders, discounted at cost of equity → equity value.

blocks.title: Should you add back stock-based comp?
blocks.body:
Genuinely debated. Adding it back (treating it as non-cash) inflates FCF unless you also account for the future dilution. Conservative practice treats SBC as a cash cost, since the company would otherwise pay it in cash. Know both sides.

**Interview answer:** "It's debated. It's non-cash, but it's a real cost through dilution, so the conservative approach treats it as a cash expense."

blocks.title: How do you treat one-time items?
blocks.teaser: Exclude non-recurring items (restructuring, litigation) from projected cash flows, since the DCF should reflect ongoing operations.
